extraction.name: MMMU: Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11,550 college-level multimodal questions designed to evaluate expert-level perception, subject knowledge, and deliberate reasoning in multimodal foundation models. It covers six disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 image types, with interleaved text and images. It includes 10,861 multiple-choice questions and 689 open-ended questions.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue et al. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4 [cs.CL], 13 June 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The collection began by selecting university subjects in which visual inputs commonly provide valuable information, resulting in 30 subjects across six disciplines. Over 50 university students, including coauthors specializing in these subjects, manually collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions using their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to use diverse sources, respect copyright and licensing restrictions, avoid sources prohibiting copying or redistribution, and prefer questions whose answers were not immediately accessible. Approximately 13,000 questions were initially collected and subsequently cleaned and filtered to produce 11,550 questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Explanations are included only if they exist; the dataset statistics report 2,035 questions with an explanation, representing 17.62% of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, free online resources, and other study materials. Some questions were newly created by annotators based on their subject expertise.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Authors corrected formatting deviations and typographical errors. Potential duplicate questions identified through lexical overlap and source URL similarity were manually reviewed and removed. Approximately 10% of collected questions classified as very easy were excluded because they did not meet the benchmark's difficulty criteria.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Collected samples were standardized into separate JSON files containing question type, question text, answer options where applicable, correct answer, difficulty, and explanation where available. Samples followed the naming convention subject_{Number}.json, and images followed image_{QuesNum}_{ImageNum}.png. Images were interleaved with question, option, or explanation text using file paths. Quality control included duplicate detection and removal, format and typo checking, and exclusion of very easy questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Subject-specialist university students and coauthors collected and annotated questions. Guidelines required English-language, college-level questions containing one or more images, without ambiguity, answerable by a single option or a short answer. Annotators recorded question type, question text, answer options for multiple-choice items, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanations if available. Authors categorized questions as very easy, easy, medium, or hard, and excluded very easy items. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and adherence to guidelines, with regular random-sample audits specified in the protocol.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification developed by Tianyu Zheng.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ambiguous or unclear instances were flagged for detailed review and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized annotation approach. A secondary review team checked annotation quality and guideline adherence. The analysis of 150 randomly sampled GPT-4V error cases attributed 2% of those errors to annotation errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including coauthors, specializing in the selected majors and drawn from various disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The annotation protocol specifies regular audits of random dataset samples to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Xiang Yue led the dataset release. The paper provides a version change log for V1 through V4 and a live-updating results leaderboard, but does not specify a dataset update schedule or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotation protocol instructs annotators to avoid collecting questions containing any private information and to comply with privacy laws and ethical standards in data handling.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to help monitor progress toward Expert AGI. The paper discusses how Expert AGI could reach the substitution threshold for human labor in many industries, creating significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption, making monitoring this progress societally important.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The focus on college-level subjects is not sufficient to establish Expert AGI: there is no direct mapping between MMMU performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI should tackle. Subjects such as law and linguistics were excluded because enough relevant multimodal problems were difficult to find. The paper acknowledges potential manual-curation biases and annotation inaccuracies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of multimodal foundation models and text-only language-model baselines on perception, subject knowledge, and reasoning. The dataset is split into a 150-question few-shot development set with five questions per subject, a 900-question validation set for hyperparameter selection and prompt engineering, and a 10,500-question test set. The development set is also used for in-context learning examples. Evaluation uses micro-averaged accuracy and rule-based answer matching for multiple-choice and concise open-ended questions. Strong performance is proposed as a necessary but not sufficient criterion for Expert AGI.
